summary: A phase distribution must account for every trial in the sample it is printed beside. Trials the registry posts with no phase at all are observational studies, and they count as N/A — the same answer phaseDisplay already gives such a trial for the Phase column, so the summary and the rendered rows agree. This is not the empty-distribution case that phase-key-always-present-on-trial-shaped-json deliberately left alone: that entry is about an empty list meaning no distribution was computed, while this is about a non-empty list silently summing to less than the sample. The observational/interventional distinction is not lost, it is carried by study_type.
reason: Every tally ranged over t.Phases with no guard, so a trial with an empty Phases array entered zero buckets and vanished. Measured on a live compare: semaglutide's distribution summed to 255 against a stated sample_size of 300, tirzepatide's to 244 against 282, with no bucket accounting for the difference.
validated_outcome: Over a ten-trial corpus of six phased, two NA and two phaseless trials, the distribution sums to ten and the N/A bucket holds four. Mutation-checked on the one tally reachable without a network client: negating the guard in buildTrialListView drops the sum to 8, the N/A bucket to 2, and leaves an all-observational corpus with zero buckets. The other three tallies sit inside RunE behind a live client; the guard is identical and verified statically to sit directly ahead of each range loop.
